title: The Live Safehouse
premise: Paloma Marchetti, a whistle-blower who testified against a transnational arms syndicate, has survived five years in witness relocation under four names — until a burner phone rings with the voice of her dead handler, Elias, who is alive, compromised, and holding the ledger that proves the syndicate bought protection inside three governments. Hunted by the assassin Kestrel and betrayed by the very marshals meant to protect her, Paloma must smuggle the ledger to a journalist across a border whose checkpoint rotations are the only window she'll get. She trades her own safety — and Elias's life — for the truth, ending with the ledger published, Kestrel walking free on a technicality, and Paloma choosing a fifth name she writes herself.
about_author: Juniper Yarrow is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who once audited shipping manifests for a defense contractor and now writes thrillers from a coastal town she refuses to name. Her novels are known for procedural precision, morally compromised protagonists, and endings that cost their heroes something real.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Paloma, living as 'Ruth Calloway' in a rain-gray Oregon town, follows her rigid safety rituals — same groceries, same routes, no attachments. A small kindness to a neighbor nearly breaks her cover. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the suffocating loneliness of a life built entirely on avoidance.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Her quarterly check-in with the marshal service goes wrong: new contact, new protocols, questions that feel like interrogation. She notices her file has been accessed from a city she's never lived in. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: creeping realization that the system protecting her is rotting from inside.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: A burner phone she buried five years ago — Elias's emergency line — rings from inside her wall. The voice is unmistakably his. He says three words: 'The ledger survived.' Then a click, then silence. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by hope, and the terror of both.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: In a Milan hotel, the assassin Kestrel receives a contract: a woman, four names, one ledger. We see his meticulous method — he studies victims like texts, reads their habits as confessions. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: cold professionalism laced with an unsettling curiosity about the woman who got away once before.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Living Voice
chapters.summary: Paloma follows the phone's cryptic coordinates to a storage unit in Portland. Inside: half the ledger, a photo of Elias alive last month, and a note warning that her marshal contact is syndicate-owned. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: vertigo — the ground under five years of survival dissolves.

chapters.title: The Marshal's Debt
chapters.summary: Deputy Marshal Corinne Voss, Paloma's original handler, is shown being leaned on by a syndicate lawyer who knows too much about her debts. Voss stalls, buys time, makes a call she shouldn't. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: a good person discovering how cheaply her loyalty was purchased.

chapters.title: Running Toward the Fire
chapters.summary: Paloma breaks her own cardinal rule and travels, using a smuggler contact from her old life to reach Boise, where Elias's message says he's held. The burner rings: wrong city, new instructions, a test. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the intoxicating danger of acting instead of hiding.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: A syndicate board scene: American intelligence, an Italian ministry, and a private military contractor all hold pieces of the ledger's exposure. They agree the witness is now more dangerous alive. POV: antagonist (the syndicate's fixer, Adeyemi). Emotional beat: banal, bureaucratic evil deciding a life in a boardroom.

chapters.title: The Test
chapters.summary: The phone leads Paloma to a motel where Kestrel is waiting — not to kill her, but to verify she's the real courier. They speak for the first time in five years; he was the failed hit that started her testimony. He lets her go, and neither knows why. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: recognition between two people shaped by the same crime.

chapters.title: Elias, Mostly
chapters.summary: Paloma finds Elias in a syndicate safehouse — alive but broken, his memory surgically unreliable. He gives her the ledger's second half and a key: the border checkpoint at Sweetgrass rotates shifts at 04:00, and one rotation is bought. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: love rekindled against the wreckage of what was done to him.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Costs
chapters.summary: The full ledger names Voss's handler, an Italian senator, and a contractor executive — and it names Paloma as its author, meaning publication destroys her protection forever. Elias begs her to burn it and run with him. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly, with no clean answer.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss, ordered to deliver Paloma's location, instead feeds the syndicate a false trail and burns her own career in the process. She calls Paloma for the first time in three years: 'Sweetgrass. 04:00. Don't trust the second car.' POV: Voss. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the price of everything she was.

chapters.title: The Long Drive
chapters.summary: Paloma and Elias drive north through Montana in a stolen car, the ledger digitized and hidden in three places. Kestrel picks up their trail and, curiously, doesn't report it immediately. POV: alternating Paloma/Kestrel. Emotional beat: tenderness under pursuit; the assassin's obsession turning to doubt.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: In a Great Falls diner, Paloma meets Dana Okafor, the investigative journalist who first broke her testimony. Dana can publish — if the ledger reaches her verified, and if Paloma goes on record again, on camera, as herself. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the terrifying arithmetic of becoming visible.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Border Town
chapters.summary: The second car at Sweetgrass isn't Voss's — it's Adeyemi's fixers. Voss arrives wounded, having been set up. A firefight in the checkpoint lot; Elias takes a bullet shielding Paloma. Kestrel watches from the ridge, rifle raised, and does not fire. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and bloody.

chapters.title: Checkpoint, 04:00
chapters.summary: With Elias dying and the bought rotation closing, Paloma crosses on foot through the freight lane while Voss holds off the fixers and is arrested. Kestrel intercepts her on the Canadian side — and instead of killing her, hands her the syndicate's kill order, signed, as evidence. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the assassin choosing a side, or at least choosing her.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: In a safehouse outside Calgary, Paloma records her testimony with Dana — real name, real face, the whole architecture of the syndicate's protection. Elias survives surgery but may never walk without help. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief and resolve braided together; she speaks her fourth name aloud and lets it go.

chapters.title: The Machines Turn
chapters.summary: Publication detonates. Three governments scramble, the senator resigns, the contractor's stock collapses, and Adeyemi initiates cleanup — including Kestrel. Voss, in custody, trades testimony for Paloma's immunity. POV: multiple (Voss, Adeyemi, Dana). Emotional beat: the truth landing like weather, indifferent to who it drowns.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel, now hunted by his own employers, delivers his contract archive to Dana — every job, every client, five years of it. He and Paloma meet once more; he refuses thanks and refuses absolution. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: a killer seeking not forgiveness but usefulness.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Last Meeting
chapters.summary: Adeyemi attempts to negotiate immunity through back channels and is arrested at the airport when the Italian ministry sacrifices him to survive. The boardroom evil dissolves into paperwork and blame. POV: antagonist. Emotional beat: the banal machine devouring its own operator.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Months later, Paloma — legally restored, publicly named, unemployable and free — visits Elias in rehabilitation. She registers a fifth name, one she chooses rather than one assigned. They are not promised anything; they choose each other anyway. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet, earned tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Live Safehouse
chapters.summary: A final scene: Paloma teaches a witness-protection seminar for whistle-blowers, telling them the truth the program won't — that no safehouse is a place, that safety is people who refuse to look away. The burner phone rings one last time; she lets it ring out, smiling. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: survival transformed into purpose; the price paid, and worth it.
